target.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR2/6 in the durable-core series and the first implementation slice.
It is stacked conceptually after the docs-only architecture gate in #107375.

GitHub cannot use a fork-only PR1 head as the base of an upstream PR, so this
submission is cumulative against `release/2026.7.1`. The implementation-only
delta is available in the [PR1-to-PR2 compare](https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/openclaw-durable-release-head-pr1-rfc-20260714...codex/durable-core-pr2-storage-v2):
16 files, 7,103 additions, and 10 deletions. The cumulative upstream surface is
20 files, 7,632 additions, and 10 deletions.

## What Problem This Solves

Official 7.1 has durable owner-specific tables but no optional shared boundary
for generic execution evidence, wake obligations, delivery-attempt evidence,
uncertainty, correlations, and bounded payload references. This slice adds
only that residual storage while preserving existing owner authority and
leaving disabled installations untouched.

## Exact base and head

- Official base: `release/2026.7.1` at
  `0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`.
- PR1 RFC head included in this cumulative branch:
  `5b8dfa9aade`.
- Exact PR2 head: `7cda8c7ab829f42ec4a8faf2ed6f62d52596695b`.
- The head is a direct descendant of the exact official base; no 7.1
  correction commit is reverted.

## What this slice adds

- An explicitly opened residual schema inside the existing shared
  `openclaw.sqlite` owner.
- A typed SQLite/Kysely store with explicit transaction composition.
- Read-only schema opening and fail-closed future-version preflight.
- Shared database handle/lease lifecycle that preserves existing state owners.
- Generated Kysely types plus naming and raw-SQL guardrails.

This PR adds no public durable configuration, starts no worker, integrates no
agent front door, dispatches no wake, exposes no Gateway/CLI method, and claims
no external delivery. Runtime configuration moves to PR3, where worker and
intake code consume it rather than leaving accepted settings inactive.

## Owner-first schema decision

Existing official 7.1 owners remain authoritative: `task_runs`,
`task_delivery_state`, `flow_runs`, `subagent_runs`,
`delivery_queue_entries`, `state_leases`, session/ACP/restart owners, audit,
and diagnostics.

When a future consumer explicitly opens the durable store, this slice adds
exactly ten residual tables:

1. `durable_execution_records`
2. `durable_event_evidence`
3. `durable_execution_steps`
4. `durable_payload_refs`
5. `durable_run_correlations`
6. `durable_timer_obligations`
7. `durable_signal_evidence`
8. `wake_obligations`
9. `delivery_attempt_evidence`
10. `uncertainty_facts`

There is no second migration ledger, mode table, result-mailbox table, generic
dedupe ledger, cleanup table, or duplicated task/flow/subagent lifecycle. The
existing `schema_meta` owner receives one `durable_runtime` version row.

## Safety properties proved

- Normal shared-state bootstrap creates no durable schema metadata or durable
  table; this slice adds no public durable setting that could imply inactive
  behavior.
- Read-only inspection never creates or migrates state.
- A future durable schema version fails before DDL, metadata updates, or
  backfill.
- Explicit initialization upgrades a real official 7.1 shared database while
  preserving canonical owner rows, including an existing `state_leases` row.
- Durable writes can join a caller-composed shared SQLite transaction and roll
  back atomically.
- Shared handles remain open while another lease is active, do not checkpoint
  prematurely, and reopen cleanly after final close.
- Terminal mutation guards, source-owner/ref requirements, dedupe keys, bounded
  metadata, and lease fencing are enforced by the store.
- Raw SQLite remains limited to explicit schema/bootstrap and store-lifecycle
  boundaries; JSON extraction uses a closed-path Kysely helper.
- The standalone storage slice uses upstream's optional Knip allowlist for
  files that Linux cannot reach until later stack wiring. It adds no public
  config type or plugin SDK export budget.

## Evidence

Run on `7cda8c7ab829f42ec4a8faf2ed6f62d52596695b`:

- `pnpm tsgo:all` - passed across all workspace projects.
- Focused durable/shared-state matrix - 5 files passed; 55 tests passed,
  1 skipped.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` - generated schema/types match.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` - Kysely guardrails OK.
- `pnpm check:durable-canonical-naming` - passed across 25 files.
- Scoped type-aware oxlint over every changed script/config/store source - passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` - passed on all matched changed files.
- Exact tooling regressions for dead-code allowlisting and the plugin SDK
  surface budget - 2 files passed; 24 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` - passed for the cumulative RFC docs.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

The focused matrix includes enabled/disabled initialization, exact table
inventory, canonical-row preservation, future-version rejection, transaction
rollback, terminal immutability, wake claim fencing, close/reopen persistence,
shared-handle lifecycle, query plans, and the closed JSON-path no-silence
diagnostic regression.

Redacted runtime probe output from the exact head (temporary database only):

```json
{"head":"7cda8c7ab829f42ec4a8faf2ed6f62d52596695b","proof":"disabled-normal-bootstrap","canonicalOwnerRows":1,"durableTables":0}
{"proof":"fresh-explicit-open","durableSchemaVersion":1,"durableTables":10}
{"proof":"upgrade-existing-official-state","canonicalOwner":"official-7.1","canonicalOwnerRows":1,"durableSchemaVersion":1,"durableTables":10,"primarySchemaVersion":1}
{"proof":"close-reopen-read-only","events":1,"runs":1,"schemaVersion":1}
```

The probe creates an official shared-state database, inserts one canonical
`state_leases` owner row, verifies normal bootstrap has zero durable tables,
opens the durable store explicitly, writes one run/event, closes it, and
reopens read-only. Its reproducible assertions are covered by the focused
tests above.

## Review and stack gate

- #107375 remains the architecture/RFC gate.
- #110143 is closed and superseded; this branch does not reuse its broad schema
  or runtime boundary.
- The five beta3 proof PRs remain untouched as archives.
- PR3 will not be submitted until both PR1 and this PR reach at least
  `rating: platinum hermit`. Later branches already exist on the fork only so
  their ancestry and proof can be prepared without bypassing that gate.

## Non-claims

- No default-on durable behavior.
- No claim that storage alone prevents every silent agent outcome.
- No arbitrary semantic replay or exactly-once external side effect.
- No public mutation API and no claim that queue acceptance proves user
  delivery.

target.title: fix(discord): keep code fences intact when rebalancing reasoning italics
target.body:
Closes #102911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a code delimiter, the italics rebalancer could prepend `_` (breaking `_```python` / `_~~~` / `_`code``) or leave unmatched trailing `_` on continuation chunks.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` still closes/reopens reasoning italics so each Discord message stays independently balanced. When the next chunk starts with a code delimiter:

1. Do **not** prepend `_` onto the code opener.
2. Reopen italics **after** the leading fenced or inline code span when later reasoning text continues.
3. Drop a lone trailing `_` on pure-code continuations.
4. Only append a closing `_` when the chunk actually opened reasoning italics.

The leading code-span scanner reuses the chunker’s fence grammar (`FENCE_RE` / `parseFenceLine`):

- backtick **or tilde** fences (` ``` ` / `~~~`)
- optional **0–3 space** indent
- **longer** closing markers (same char, length ≥ open)

Regression tests assert exact second-chunk output and even `_` counts for backtick, tilde, indented, longer-close, inline, and pure-code cases.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer break markdown fences at chunk boundaries, including tilde and indented fences, and each chunk keeps balanced reasoning italics when text continues after code.

## Evidence

### Focused tests
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

### Production-path harness (`chunkDiscordText` → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`)

**Current main (before):** second chunk could start with `_```python…` (broken fence).

**This patch (exact second chunks):**
```
tilde:      "~~~python\nprint(1)\n~~~\n_more_"
indent:     "  ```python\nprint(1)\n  ```\n_more_"
long-close: "```python\nprint(1)\n````\n_more_"
```
All chunks have even `_` counts; openers are not prefixed with `_`.

### Changed-lane gates
```
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs  # PASS
pnpm test:changed  # PASS (extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts, 24 tests)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Discord reasoning-italics rebalance protects code-leading openers using the full chunker fence grammar and keeps per-message `_` balance.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node 24; production helper `chunkDiscordText`. Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: with `maxLines: 10`, a reasoning body whose continuation starts at a fenced block produced `_```…` on main; incomplete parsers also missed tilde / indented / longer-close forms.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx` harness for tilde, indented, and longer-close fixtures
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts`
  3. `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`
  4. `pnpm test:changed`
- Evidence after fix: exact second-chunk outputs above; 24/24 tests green including tilde, indented, longer-close, inline, and pure-code cases.
- Control check: normal multi-chunk reasoning still reopens with leading `_` on non-code continuations.
- Observed result after fix: supported fence forms stay intact and each emitted message remains delimiter-balanced.
- What was not tested: live Discord API delivery in a real workspace (source-level path is the production chunker used before send).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation, tests, and proof were verified against ClawSweeper review findings on #103166 (balance code-leading chunks; reuse full fence grammar).

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): bound Anthropic Vertex ADC credential read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`canReadAnthropicVertexAdc` in `src/plugin-sdk/anthropic-vertex-auth-presence.ts` reads the entire GCP ADC credentials file via unbounded `fs.readFileSync(credentialsPath, "utf8")` solely to check whether the file is readable — its contents are discarded. The path comes from `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (an external, user-controlled env var) or the default gcloud ADC path, so a misconfigured or oversized file triggers an unbounded memory read just to report `true`.

The provider-local copy of this exact logic in `extensions/anthropic-vertex/region.ts` was already bounded with `tryReadSecretFileSync` + a 1 MiB limit in #109260 ("reject oversized credential files in remaining readers"). This standalone plugin-sdk preflight helper is a duplicate that sweep missed.

This PR mirrors the region.ts bound: replace the unbounded `readFileSync` with `tryReadSecretFileSync(..., { maxBytes: 1 MiB, rejectHardlinks: false })`, wrapped in `try/catch` (the helper throws `FsSafeError` on oversize) so an oversized credential file is rejected instead of slurped into memory. Presence-check semantics are unchanged for normal-sized files.

## Evidence

Proof script run with Node 22 + tsx (`hasAnthropicVertexAvailableAuth` against real temp files):

```
ADC read bound: 1048576 bytes (1024 KiB)

[1] Small ADC file (normal credential):
    size:  32 bytes
    NEW hasAnthropicVertexAvailableAuth: true  (expected true)

[2] Oversized ADC file (2 MiB, exceeds bound):
    size:  2097153 bytes
    OLD unbounded readFileSync:           true  (read entire 2097153-byte file, returned true)
    NEW hasAnthropicVertexAvailableAuth: false  (expected false: bound rejects oversize)

RESULT: normal read preserved = true; oversized rejected by bound = true; old code read it fully = true
PASS
```

- Normal-sized ADC file → still detected (`true`), no regression.
- Oversized 2 MiB ADC file → rejected (`false`) by the 1 MiB bound; the old unbounded code read the entire file and returned `true`.
- Existing unicode-path test still passes; preflight test still asserts no `existsSync` preflight; added a regression test for oversize rejection.
- Local precheck: vitest 3/3 green, `tsgo:core:test` clean, oxlint clean.

target.title: fix(ui): Realtime Talk hangs when Google Live connections stall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI users starting Realtime Talk with Google Live could remain stuck in the connecting state when the browser WebSocket never opened or opened without Google ever completing protocol setup. During that stall, the microphone, camera stream, input meter, and both audio contexts could remain active indefinitely. A socket error or close before readiness could leave the same resources active until the user manually dismissed the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser WebSocket construction has no caller-configurable startup deadline, so the Google Live transport now owns a 30-second deadline covering the full startup phase through the current socket's Google `setupComplete` frame. This matches the existing Realtime Talk WebRTC setup deadline while using the provider-specific readiness signal instead of treating the lower-level WebSocket `open` event as ready.

Timeout, error, and close paths report the transport error and stop the current socket lifecycle exactly once. Captured-socket checks before and after asynchronous message decoding keep stale socket events from clearing a replacement attempt's timer or emitting readiness for it. The conflict resolution with the merged Gemini Live video work preserves camera-frame shutdown, media-track release, and `onVideoStream(null)` cleanup.

## User Impact

Google Live Realtime Talk now fails with a clear error instead of connecting forever when either the WebSocket handshake or Google protocol setup stalls. Failed, closed, and timed-out attempts release the microphone, camera, input meter, socket, and both AudioContext instances without waiting for another user action.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3614ee6fa9287672c58763ffeecb048819a59f9c`, based on `8020dd3e0830ead01dc81c8a446444078315b63d`. The branch was rebuilt from current `main` using only the two substantive PR commits, removing two historical merge commits and resolving the sole conflict with #109719's video lifecycle.

- Node 24.15.0 focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-google-live.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-google-live-video.test.ts` - 2 files and 28 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves both pre-open and post-open/no-`setupComplete` timeout paths. The video-enabled path verifies audio and camera tracks stop, the socket closes, and `onVideoStream` receives `null` after the combined stream.
- A separate regression proves that the current socket's `setupComplete` frame clears the deadline and emits `listening`, so a healthy session is not timed out later.
- Existing terminal-path coverage verifies `error -> close`, direct pre-open `close`, and manual stop release resources and clear timers once.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. Stable patch ID after the final rebase: `74ccb1db30be21ec23a1414f6568aa584fb8044a`.
- Bounded live observation against Google's documented constrained WebSocket endpoint with an intentionally invalid probe token: `{"reason":"watchdog","elapsedMs":15060,"readyState":2,"events":[{"type":"open","ms":812}]}`. It establishes the specific post-open/no-application-readiness state now bounded by the patch.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the rebuilt exact patch found no P1/P2 issue and judged the timeout plus video cleanup conflict resolution correct after checking the full transport, callers, siblings, current-main video behavior, and both focused suites.

Proof gap: the live probe was not an authenticated Google Live success session. This environment has no `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` and cannot provide redacted real-browser proof of the patched visible error and media/context cleanup, so that remains for a credentialed browser run or maintainer review. The focused tests exercise those exact cleanup effects deterministically.

Remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment, so the focused Node 24 run used the repository's allowed local fallback.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.

target.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR1/6 in the proposed durable-core series. It is documentation/RFC
only and asks maintainers to accept, narrow, or reject one owner-first
cross-owner boundary. It does not land runtime, schema, worker, delivery,
Gateway, CLI, or owner-control behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Official 7.1 lifecycle owners are individually durable, but they cannot by
themselves answer cross-owner attention, handoff-evidence, replay-safety, and
uncertainty questions after restart or deferred execution. This RFC defines a
narrow residual boundary for those facts without replacing existing owners.

## Named contributor owner decision

For this proposed stack:

- implementation owner: @mjnkao;
- optional durable-schema migration owner: @mjnkao;
- selected contributor direction: **narrow residual boundary**.

That direction keeps all existing official 7.1 lifecycle owners authoritative
and adds only source-backed cross-owner facts they cannot safely own alone. It
resolves contributor-side implementation and migration ownership; it does not
claim upstream maintainer sponsorship or make this RFC an accepted contract.

## Verified official 7.1 owner comparison

The proposal was re-audited and rebased onto exact
`release/2026.7.1` head
`0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`.

Current owner evidence includes:

- task lifecycle and delivery state:
  `src/tasks/task-registry.store.sqlite.ts` and task owner APIs;
- Task Flow lifecycle/revisions/waits:
  `src/tasks/task-flow-registry.store.sqlite.ts`;
- subagent lifecycle, result capture, timeout, cleanup, and final-delivery
  retry: `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` plus registry APIs;
- delivery queue lifecycle and recovery:
  `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and
  `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts`;
- shared schema and `state_leases` authority:
  `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts`;
- persisted session handoff:
  `src/infra/session-delivery-queue-storage.ts` and recovery APIs;
- restart/boot evidence:
  `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts`, `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, and
  `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts`;
- ACP/session/binding owners remain authoritative through their existing
  session, replay, and conversation-binding APIs.

The proposal does not mirror or replace any of those lifecycles.

## Residual boundary proposed

The remaining gap is cross-owner consistency after restart, deferred work, or
an ambiguous handoff:

1. Which existing owner fact requires attention, and from whom?
2. What handoff or delivery was attempted, and what was actually proven?
3. Is replay safe, denied, or uncertain after a possible side effect?
4. How are related owner records correlated and inspected without taking over
   their lifecycle authority?

The candidate residual schema is exactly ten enabled-only tables:

1. `durable_execution_records`
2. `durable_event_evidence`
3. `durable_execution_steps`
4. `durable_payload_refs`
5. `durable_run_correlations`
6. `durable_timer_obligations`
7. `durable_signal_evidence`
8. `wake_obligations`
9. `delivery_attempt_evidence`
10. `uncertainty_facts`

Generic execution records are allowed only when no task, flow, subagent, or
other lifecycle owner exists. There is no second task/flow/subagent ledger,
result-mailbox table, dedupe ledger, cleanup table, mode table, decision table,
or migration ledger. The existing shared SQLite file and `schema_meta` owner
remain authoritative.

## Compatibility and public boundary

- Durable runtime is explicit opt-in; worker authority is separately gated.
- Disabled paths create no DB/schema side effect and do not eagerly load the
  recovery/owner-adapter module graph.
- Future durable schema versions fail closed before mutation.
- `handoff_accepted` means only an exact internal owner/queue boundary; it is
  not attached-session consumption, user delivery, or external transport
  success.
- The initial additive public vocabulary is `durable.*` Gateway inspection and
  `openclaw durable` CLI inspection.
- The initial stack exposes no public acknowledge, retry, resume, abandon,
  replay, or direct owner mutation.
- Model strength, profile, skill, prompt wording, and context-window size are
  outside the correctness boundary.

## Follow-on proof

Replacement PR2 is #111121. It provides the concrete enabled-only shared-state
foundation and exact schema proof while remaining cumulative against the same
official base because GitHub cannot use a fork-only PR1 head as an upstream PR
base.

PR3 will not be submitted until both PR1 and PR2 reach at least
`rating: platinum hermit`. Fork-only PR3-PR6 branches are preparation artifacts,
not submitted bypasses of this gate.

The obsolete #110143 remains closed. The five beta3 PRs #104246, #104327,
#105660, #105844, and #106443 remain untouched proof archives.

## Evidence

- Exact PR head:
  `5b8dfa9aade`.
- Direct parent series begins at exact official base
  `0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`.
- Surface: 4 documentation files, 529 additions, no source/config/schema
  changes.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` - passed.
- `pnpm format:docs:check` - passed across 689 docs files.
- `pnpm lint:docs` - 0 issues across 689 files.
- `git diff --check` and exact ancestry/diff inspection - passed.

Runtime proof is not applicable to this docs-only RFC. Executable storage proof
belongs to #111121 and later runtime proof remains gated by the accepted scope.

## Maintainer decision requested

1. **Accept the narrow residual boundary** and sponsor serial implementation
   review after this gate.
2. **Narrow it further** by naming a residual fact that an existing owner can
   safely represent.
3. **Reject a shared residual layer** and require each cross-owner gap to be
   expressed entirely through existing owner-specific APIs.

Until maintainers decide, these pages remain provisional and unlisted.

target.title: fix(tlon): preserve shutdown when body cancellation fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where closing a Tlon client could leave two process-level unhandled rejections if cancellation of the unsubscribe and channel-delete response bodies failed, even though shutdown and guarded response release otherwise completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both shutdown response cancellations now observe and suppress their own cleanup failures while retaining the existing fire-and-forget timing and `finally`-owned releases. The risk is limited to Tlon shutdown cleanup; open PR #108168 touches reconnect-delay cancellation in the same module but not these two response cleanup sites.

## User Impact

Tlon channel shutdown can finish cleanly without secondary response-body cancellation failures leaking into the process.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(update): keep repair JSON output parseable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw update repair --json` could receive exit code 0 while stdout contained Doctor and nested gateway-service output before the final result. Consumers parsing the complete stdout stream would therefore fail even though the command reported success.

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON update finalization now gives its embedded Doctor run a stderr-backed runtime and UI stream. Doctor scopes terminal notes to that stream across async work and forwards it through gateway-service stage, install, and restart operations. Human and non-JSON Doctor callers retain their existing runtime and stdout defaults.

The routing stays at the embedding update finalizer and Doctor lifecycle boundaries instead of monkey-patching process-global stdout.

## User Impact

Automation can parse the complete stdout from `openclaw update repair --json` as one JSON value. Human update-repair behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Final exact candidate: `256542f28e268f20bb6257ec540f8eee1974bff4` over public main `047232bd16e407cf53762eb6ffa80d400b1d249e`.

Validated with Node `24.15.0` and pnpm `11.2.2`:

- scoped terminal-note and terminal-restore output: 6/6
- real Doctor/Clack UI composition: 1/1
- gateway-service repair lifecycle: 49/49
- changed JSON and human update-finalization cases: 6/6
- targeted oxfmt: 10/10 files
- targeted core oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- max-lines ratchet, conflict-marker, changelog-attribution, secret, dangerous-construct, and diff checks passed
- final worktree clean

Clean-room exact-head source proof on Blaxel (`blaxel/codex:latest`, isolated HOME/state, no user config or services):

```text
source SHA: 256542f28e268f20bb6257ec540f8eee1974bff4
source archive SHA-256: 64847d975021423d98bca0096758518083895d8a87787c94841b22935e7fb2bc
command: node --import tsx src/entry.ts update repair --json
command exit: 0
full stdout JSON parse: true
stdout: 536 bytes, SHA-256 e3491c31a1c16ff884d2f400bb1813f2c7557deb768d86a881542419d3759cfb
stdout JSON: {"status":"ok","mode":"finalize",...,"postUpdate":{"doctor":{"status":"ok"},"plugins":{"status":"ok",...}}}
stderr: 10674 bytes, SHA-256 4d0e9215879a09a252c4e7d7742bf0043bced87b14deb567bb554ba21155b21a
stderr preview:
  T  OpenClaw doctor
  |
  o  UI -------------------------------+
  |  - Control UI assets are missing.  |
  o  UI -----------------------------------------------------+
  |  Building Control UI assets... (this may take a moment)  |
cleanup verified: true
```

The full captured stdout was passed directly to `JSON.parse`; the Doctor/Clack transcript above came from the separately captured stderr file. The disposable 8 GiB Linux worker completed in 273.903 seconds, cost upper-bound estimate was `$0.025199`, and provider-side deletion was verified.

The final SHA additionally covers rich-TTY error exits. Regression tests verify that finalization failures, embedded Doctor exits, and pre-mutation JSON failures route terminal reset bytes to stderr instead of appending ANSI to stdout.

The full update CLI test file and full repository build were not rerun on the final SHA; GitHub CI remains the broad verification gate.

target.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin registration transaction snapshot used a shallow clone (`{ ...value }` for object fields), leaving nested registration objects (e.g. hook/tool/config entries) shared by reference with the live registry. In-transaction nested mutations therefore survived a rollback and orphaned registers stayed in the manifest cache (#107514). The earlier shallow clone also collapsed non-plain values (e.g. `Date`) to `{}` on rollback, corrupting typed failure metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the shallow clone with a recursive deep clone that reverts nested data changes on restore. Function-valued fields and other unclonable class instances are kept by reference (registrations carry resolver/handler functions that `structuredClone` cannot clone and that are never mutated), while typed values such as `Date` keep their constructor across snapshot/restore so rollback does not corrupt failure metadata.

## User Impact

Plugin registration install/enable timeouts that roll back no longer leave orphaned registers / stale nested config, and typed registry values (e.g. `failedAt: Date`) survive rollback intact. No behavior change for successful commits.

## Evidence

Real runtime proof against the built module using a real `Date`, real functions, and the real transaction lifecycle (no mocks):

```
[nested-config-reverted]   PASS=true
[date-instance-preserved]   PASS=true
[date-value-preserved]      PASS=true
[function-preserved-callable] PASS=true
RUNTIME_PROOF_OK: typed values (Date) and callable entries survive snapshot/rollback; nested mutations revert
```

Regression tests in `src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts` cover nested-mutation rollback, `Date` preservation, and callable-entry preservation (4 tests passing). `pnpm lint` + `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

Freshness gate: `git diff origin/main` confirms the shallow clone is still present on latest `main`; no competing open PR references #107514.


### Custom-class instance identity (re-review fix)

`structuredClone` silently drops custom-class prototypes, so the snapshot helper now keeps typed instances (non-`Date` class instances) by reference when a structured clone would lose the prototype. Real runtime proof against the built module:

```
[custom-instance-instanceof-after-rollback]  PASS=true
[custom-instance-method-callable-after-rollback] PASS=true
RUNTIME_PROOF_OK: custom-class registry values keep constructor/methods across rollback
```

target.title: fix(sessions): manual compaction deletes transcript history while claiming it was archived
target.body:
Related: #98236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines N` would permanently lose the trimmed part of their conversation history while the CLI told them it had been archived. Since the SQLite storage flip (#98236, commit 0a8e3604ba2), the manual compaction path deletes the trimmed transcript rows without writing any backup, then returns an `archived` value that is a fabricated marker string (`sqlite:<agent>:<session>:<store>.bak.<timestamp>`) pointing at nothing. The CLI prints `Archived transcript: <marker>`, so users believe the full history is recoverable when it is gone. Before the flip, manual compaction renamed the live JSONL transcript to a real `.bak.<timestamp>` file before writing the trimmed replacement, so the full pre-compaction history was always recoverable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix restores the pre-flip safety contract at the SQLite transcript writer boundary: before any rows are deleted, the complete pre-compaction transcript is exported to a real, durable archive file, and `archived` now returns that file's actual path. The archive reuses the existing session archive writer that the reset/delete lifecycle flows already use (exclusive create, 0o600, fsync file and directory, atomic rename, optional zstd), with the artifact named `<sessionId>.jsonl.bak.<timestamp>[.zst]` in the same per-agent sessions archive directory. The `.bak` shape is already recognized by the archive artifact classifiers, so cleanup and disk-budget treat it exactly like reset/delete archives. The backup is written outside any SQLite transaction; the destructive replacement then revalidates the row snapshot inside the write transaction and aborts (removing the fresh backup) if the transcript changed after the snapshot, so concurrently appended rows can never be deleted. If backup creation fails, compaction aborts with an error and every original row stays in place. Active-run and lifecycle fencing in the `sessions.compact` RPC is unchanged.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines N` is safe again: the printed `Archived transcript:` path is a real file containing every pre-compaction transcript event in order, recoverable with the same tooling that reads reset/delete archives. If the backup cannot be written, compaction fails without deleting anything instead of silently destroying history.

## Evidence

Live before/after against a real gateway and the real CLI, identical inputs. For each phase: fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, a session seeded with 7 transcript events (session header plus messages `important message 1..6`) through the production accessor, gateway started from the built dist (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --port <port>`), then `node openclaw.mjs sessions compact main --max-lines 3 --url ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --token ...`. Nothing was mocked.

Before, on pristine main 62c5a8b888:

```
$ openclaw sessions compact main --max-lines 3
Compacted session agent:main:main (kept 3 lines).
Archived transcript: sqlite:main:aaaaaaaa-...:<state>/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json.bak.2026-07-19T01-52-43.722Z

authoritative transcript rows now: 3
sessions dir unreadable: ENOENT
backup artifacts in agents/main/sessions: []
claimed archive path exists: false
```

Four transcript events were deleted, the printed "archive" is a marker string, the archive directory was never created, and no backup exists anywhere. The trimmed history is unrecoverable.

After, this patch:

```
$ openclaw sessions compact main --max-lines 3
Compacted session agent:main:main (kept 3 lines).
Archived transcript: <state>/agents/main/sessions/aaaaaaaa-...jsonl.bak.2026-07-19T02-00-59.389Z.zst

authoritative transcript rows now: 3
backup artifacts in agents/main/sessions: ["aaaaaaaa-...jsonl.bak.2026-07-19T02-00-59.389Z.zst"]
backup aaaaaaaa-...jsonl.bak.2026-07-19T02-00-59.389Z.zst: 7 events, first=session, contents include: 6 messages
claimed archive path exists: true
```

The printed path is a real file (mode 0600), and decompressing it yields all 7 pre-compaction events in order, including the 4 trimmed ones, parsed back through the shared archive reader.

Validation on the changed surface (all green locally):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts src/commands/sessions-compact.test.ts` (72 + 10 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` (21 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.conformance.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts src/config/sessions/artifacts.test.ts` (123 passed)
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files; `git diff --check` clean

Control red: with only the four production files reverted to main, the updated trim test plus the two new tests fail in `session-accessor.test.ts` (3 failed) and the updated gateway archive test fails in `server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` (1 failed); with the patch they all pass.

New regression coverage:

- accessor: trim writes a `.bak` artifact holding every original event, parseable via the archive reader; backup-write failure (archive directory path occupied by a file) leaves all rows untouched and errors; a row appended after the backup snapshot aborts the replacement with a conflict error, deletes nothing, and removes the fresh backup.
- gateway RPC: `sessions.compact` with `maxLines` returns an `archived` path that exists on disk and contains all 500 seeded pre-compaction events.
- CLI: the printed `Archived transcript:` line is exactly the RPC's `archived` path.

Not tested live: Bun runtime (plain JSONL archive fallback path, exercised by the shared writer used unchanged by reset/delete flows) and Windows.

Siblings: session reset and delete flows already archive through the same writer and are unchanged. `sessions.compact` without `--max-lines` (LLM summarization) rewrites via compaction checkpoints, not row deletion, and is unaffected.

target.title: fix(ui): teardown MCP Apps before unmount
target.body:
Related: #110515

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users leaving, replacing, or rerendering a Control UI MCP App view could have its iframe detached before the app acknowledged `ui/resource-teardown`. That could skip app cleanup during route changes, split-pane changes, virtualized transcript eviction, or explicit app teardown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The render owners now hold the outgoing subtree while each nested MCP App performs one bounded teardown, then commit the latest coalesced render. The component owns one resource generation, clears listeners/subscriptions exactly once, removes the iframe only after the teardown response or the named 250 ms timeout, and cannot let a stale teardown remove a replacement. Retained panes and rows stay mounted; only a torn-down view that survives the parent commit is restarted.

The change intentionally does not add a second host, detached-frame cache, compatibility shim, or unbounded render queue.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the complete owner/caller/callee surface and the exact `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.4` teardown contract, and addressed all accepted autoreview findings.

## User Impact

Control UI MCP Apps now receive their required teardown notification while still connected, including during rerender, view replacement, page changes, and explicit app teardown. Cleanup is bounded, replacement-safe, and does not reset the per-view prompt budget on remount. There is no visual change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-unmount.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/app/router-outlet.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts`: 159/159 passed on exact-head Testbox.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed the `coreTests, ui` lanes, including formatting, core-test/UI typechecks, and full lint.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including the Control UI production build, sidecar verification, and performance budgets.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/mcp-app-conformance.e2e.test.ts`: real system Chromium passed. The conformance host observed the Control UI teardown response before iframe detachment; standalone teardown, reload, tool, and resource flows stayed green.

target.title: fix: release stream reader lock, bound error body reads, cancel cloned body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three issues where HTTP response bodies are not properly cleaned up or bounded in failure paths:

1. **Ollama stream reader lock never released**: `response.body.getReader()` lock was never released, relying solely on implicit fetch cleanup which can delay socket reuse in some Node.js versions.
2. **HTTP error body read without byte limit**: The `readResponseBodySnippet` fallback used `response.arrayBuffer()` (and previously `response.text()`) on the body-less path, materializing the entire error body before slicing the buffer. A reverse proxy returning a multi??undred??B body could OOM the gateway before `limits.maxBytes` was applied.
3. **Firecrawl error-path body not explicitly cancelled**: After cloning and consuming a response body for JSON error parsing, the original body was not explicitly cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`: Hoist `reader = response.body.getReader()` so the `finally` block can call `reader?.releaseLock()` (defensive `try/catch`) before `await release()`. The reader no longer relies on implicit fetch cleanup.
- `src/infra/http-error-body.ts`:
  - Pre??heck `Content-Length` on body??ess responses and short??ircuit oversize declared bodies with an empty (truncated) result, never materializing the body.
  - Wrap body??ess responses in a cancelable `ReadableStream` and route them through the shared `readResponseTextPrefix` helper. The shared helper cancels the source once it has seen `limits.maxBytes` bytes, and the wrapper honors that cancel by refusing to enqueue further chunks. The old `arrayBuffer()` + `subarray` path is removed because the slice never reduced the allocated buffer.
- `extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.ts`: After the JSON-payload clone is consumed, call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` to release the underlying body.

## User Impact

Gateway and plugin processes no longer leak stream resources or risk large memory allocations on error responses. Connection pools recover faster after Ollama/Firecrawl failures, and the `http-error-body` shared fallback no longer allocates the complete body before applying `limits.maxBytes`.

## Evidence

### Acceptance criteria

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts` ??every test passes, including the new body-less safety cases (`rejects an oversize Content-Length without materializing the body`, `streams a body-less response and stops at limits.maxBytes (cancelled wrapper)`, `accepts a body-less response whose declared Content-Length fits within limits.maxBytes`).
- `pnpm test extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts` ??passes; the new `response.body?.cancel()` call is exercised by the existing `payload-success` and `payload-fail` cases.
- `pnpm test extensions/ollama` ??passes; the success path is unchanged and the cleanup `finally` block exercises `releaseLock()` on both success and error termination.

### Real behavior proof (redacted)

- **Pre-check short-circuit**: a synthetic `Response` with `body: null`, `headers: { "content-length": "10000" }`, and a `text()` that increments a counter is fed into `readResponseBodySnippet` with `maxBytes: 64`. The counter is `0` after the call and the returned string is `""`. The body is never materialized.
- **Bounded streaming read (body-less)**: a 200??yte body-less response is fed in with `maxBytes: 50`. The result has UTF?? byte length `??50` and is strictly shorter than the source. The internal `pull()` enqueues a 16 KiB chunk and stops enqueueing as soon as the shared `readResponseTextPrefix` reader cancels the source.
- **Ollama reader release**: a spy `getReader` is mounted and the stream is interrupted with a non??K response. `reader.releaseLock()` is observed in the test harness before `release()` returns.
- **Firecrawl cancel**: a `Response` whose `body.cancel()` resolves is passed through the JSON??rror branch; `cancel()` is observed and the success-path `parse` is reached when the JSON payload is valid.

### Lint and format

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passes for the three changed files.
- `pnpm exec oxlint` passes for the three changed files (no new warnings introduced).

### Note on `process/child-process` shard

The `checks-node-core-test-nondist-shard` failure visible on the latest CI run is a pre-existing `process/child-process.test.ts > drains active descendant output after the parent exits` flake that is already red on `main` (tracked by the maintainer team). It is unrelated to this PR's changed files and, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, is not fixed by contributor PRs.

target.title: feat(android): platform trust for public gateway certs + manual fingerprint pinning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app pins a TLS fingerprint for every gateway, including hosts with publicly valid certificates. For a Tailscale Funnel gateway on `*.ts.net` with a Let's Encrypt cert, that means a "fingerprint changed" re-verification prompt every 60–90 day renewal — recurring friction that trains users to click through security prompts. Separately, when the TLS probe failed with no stored pin, connecting hard-failed with no escape hatch, and a malformed stored pin silently degraded instead of failing closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Platform trust for public certs.** Before prompting, the probe performs a real handshake against the system CA store with `endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS"` and SNI. If the chain validates and the hostname matches, the connection uses platform trust — no pin stored, no prompt, renewals just work. A conservative candidate classifier (rejects `.local`, IPv4/IPv6 literals, single-label and malformed hostnames) keeps LAN endpoints on the existing pin flow.
- **Existing pins stay authoritative.** A valid public chain never silently clears a user-accepted pin. On mismatch with a system-trusted cert, the changed-pin prompt gains an explicit "Use system trust" choice; picking it clears the pin once, after which renewals are automatic. Replacing a pin always requires explicit confirmation.
- **Discovery cannot become identity.** Saved discovered endpoints still require a stored fingerprint for reconnect eligibility — mDNS advertisements are attacker-controllable on the LAN, and a DNS-shaped advertised host with the attacker's own valid cert must not inherit a saved gateway's credentials.
- **Out-of-band manual pinning.** When the probe can't capture a certificate, the trust dialog accepts a pasted SHA-256 fingerprint obtained on the gateway host (tolerates `sha256:` prefixes, colons, whitespace, case; requires 64 hex), then enforces it on connect — stronger verification than eyeball-TOFU, and an escape hatch where there was a dead end.
- Hardening along the way: malformed stored pins now fail closed at handshake time; both probe attempts share one connect+handshake budget so a TCP-accepting, TLS-stalling host cannot double probe latency; the trust decision is a closed sealed type (`SystemTrusted` / `PinnedTrust` / `PromptRequired` / `Failed`).

## User Impact

Funnel/public-cert gateways connect without fingerprint ceremony and stop re-prompting on cert renewals. LAN and IP gateways keep trust-on-first-use pinning with the existing first-seen and changed-pin dialogs. Users who deliberately pinned a public host keep their pin unless they explicitly switch. Two new user-facing strings, translated across all 21 locales.

## Evidence

- `GatewayTlsTest` (trust-decision matrix incl. supersession rows, candidate classifier, fingerprint normalizer, probe-budget splitting), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest`, `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest`: green on both Play and ThirdParty flavors (14 + 51 + 2 per flavor).
- `:app:ktlintCheck`, `android-app-i18n` check, `git diff --check`: green.
- Structured autoreview: three rounds; four accepted findings fixed (two P1s — discovery-eligibility identity binding, silent pin supersession — plus fail-closed pin handling and probe-latency amplification); final round clean: "consistently adds Android platform trust for eligible DNS gateways while preserving existing certificate pins."
- All `resolveTlsParams` call sites verified `allowTOFU=false`, so the system-trust path connects with platform trust and real hostname verification (no TOFU fallback).

target.title: fix(telegram): surface draft stream delivery failures at warn level
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Telegram draft/preview streaming fails — `sendMessage`/`editMessageText` rejections, a missing message id from `sendMessage`, or preview cleanup failures — the failure is reported only through `logVerbose`. In the default configuration these lines never reach the logs: the preview stream silently stops and the operator sees nothing. This is worst in `progress` stream mode, where the activity window is the only visible delivery surface, so a dead draft stream looks like the bot silently ignoring the user, with no trace to debug from.

Observed on a production gateway: intermittent "bot went quiet" reports that took a verbose-logging session to trace back to `telegram stream preview failed: ...` errors that had been happening invisibly.

Closes #111064

## Why This Change Was Made

`createTelegramDraftController` wired the draft stream's `warn` callback to `logVerbose` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts`). The failure messages themselves originate in `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts` ("telegram stream preview failed: ...", "telegram stream preview stopped (missing message id from sendMessage)", "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: ...", "telegram stream preview cleanup was not confirmed ..."), so the stream already distinguishes warn-worthy failures from verbose progress logging — the dispatch wiring just discarded that distinction.

The fix routes the `warn` callback through the plugin's standard subsystem logger (`createSubsystemLogger("telegram/draft-stream")`) at warn level, attaching `lane` (answer/reasoning), `chatId`, and `threadId` so a failure can be tied to a specific chat and delivery lane. The verbose `log` callback is unchanged, and no delivery behavior changes — this is logging-only.

## User Impact

Operators now see draft/preview delivery failures in default logs with enough context to identify the affected chat and lane, instead of a silently stalled bot. No change to message delivery, retries, or stream behavior.

## Evidence

- New test in the existing dispatch failure harness: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.draft-failures-progress.test.ts` — "routes draft stream failures to the warn-level telegram logger with lane context" proves the warn callback passed to `createTelegramDraftStream` emits on the `telegram/draft-stream` subsystem logger at warn level with `{ lane, chatId, threadId }`, not on the verbose path.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.draft-failures-progress.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts` — 103 passed.
- `.../bot-message-dispatch.draft-finalization.test.ts .../bot-message-dispatch.draft-rotation.test.ts` — 27 passed.
- Extensions tsgo lane: no errors in touched files (only pre-existing, unrelated `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors present at base).
- The equivalent patch has been running on a production gateway since 2026-07-11 and has surfaced real preview failures that were previously invisible.

This PR was AI-assisted (implemented with Claude Code; reviewed by the operator).


This fix was developed with AI assistance; the change and its validation were reviewed by the submitting author.


## Runtime evidence (added after ClawSweeper review)

### Runtime proof: induced Telegram outage, BEFORE vs AFTER

**Harness.** A driver (tsx against this checkout) runs the real production bundle end to end: `createTelegramDraftController` from `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts` builds its draft lanes, the lanes construct the real `createTelegramDraftStream` from `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts`, and the `warn`/`log` callbacks are the module's own wiring (`logVerbose` on main; the `telegram/draft-stream` subsystem logger from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` on this branch). Logging runs at the default configuration (console level `info`, file level `info`; the state dir is isolated via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, with only `logging.file` pointed into the harness directory). The single mocked piece is the Bot API transport: `sendMessage` succeeds once (the preview lands as `message_id=4242` in synthetic chat `987654321`, topic `777`), then the connection dies — every subsequent `editMessageText` and the teardown `deleteMessage` reject with `ECONNRESET` (`socket hang up`). The stream makes 4 edit attempts (3 retryable, then terminal stop) plus 1 cleanup delete attempt.

For BEFORE, the harness swaps in the `origin/main` version of `bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts` (the git blob hash printed inside each capture proves which version ran); for AFTER it restores the branch file. Same driver, same induced failure. Excerpts below are verbatim except: the `date:`/`node:` header lines are omitted, `[worktree]` substitutes the local checkout path, `hostname` is redacted, and gateway-log `_meta` is trimmed (`…`) to its level fields. All chat/thread/message ids are synthetic harness values.

**BEFORE — origin/main, default log config: the outage is invisible.** Four failed preview edits and a failed cleanup delete produce zero operator-visible output, and the gateway log file stays empty — the dead progress stream looks like the bot silently ignoring the user:

```

(gateway log file is empty / was not written)

**BEFORE — same run with verbose enabled (honesty check).** The failure text exists, but only as unlabeled verbose console chatter, and still never reaches the gateway log file:

```

target.title: fix: stop selected channel sessions from WebChat
target.body:
Supersedes #101495

Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a running channel session in Control UI could not stop it with `/stop` or the stop action when that run was started outside the browser. The selected session appeared active, but the browser had no local run ID, so the stop request did not reach that channel session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser-owned runs still use the existing run-ID-targeted `chat.abort` path. When no browser-local run ID exists, Control UI now sends `sessions.abort` for the exact selected session. After agent/session resolution and existing authorization, the Gateway clears that non-global session's queued successors and aborts its exact persisted embedded/reply run before signaling tracked runs, preventing a draining run from starting queued work.

This rebuild is intentionally narrower than #101495: it does not scan hidden controllers or pending registries, does not widen `chat.abort` authorization, and does not fabricate a run ID for reply-only work. Foreign connection-owned chat runs and worker runs remain untouched. Canonical global scope stays on its existing `chat.abort` behavior because the shared literal `global` queue has no safe per-agent cleanup identity; this PR targets distinct channel sessions.

## User Impact

Control UI users can stop the exact selected Weixin, Telegram, or other channel session even when that work was started by the channel rather than the current browser. Other channel sessions continue running, queued work for the selected session cannot restart after the stop, and browser-owned run cancellation keeps its existing targeted behavior.

## Evidence

Current-head automated proof after rebasing onto latest `main`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-authorization.test.ts` — 19 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-agent-scope.test.ts` — 28 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts -- -t handleAbortChat` — 15 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -- -t "sends /stop to the exact selected channel session"` — 1 passed
- Core production, core test, and UI `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed for all eight changed files.
- Fresh branch autoreview completed with no accepted/actionable findings (correctness 0.93).

Prior #101495 behavior recordings are retained as scenario evidence; the automated checks above are the proof for this new head:

- [Selected channel session stops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f32135-1f1a-4f9c-b0a7-ddade5464b86)
- [Other channel sessions remain active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b78d13-90c5-416f-a354-610fef9b6c59)

target.title: Bound trajectory pointer file read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readTrajectoryPointerFile` calls `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` on session trajectory pointer files with no size limit. A corrupted pointer file can OOM the trajectory cleanup path.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern for file reads. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON metadata files, but the unbounded `readFileSync` call was a latent vulnerability. Using `readRegularFileSync` with a 1 MB cap (generous for pointer files which are typically <1 KB) prevents OOM from corrupted pointer files.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON objects (<1 KB typically); a 1 MB cap is more than sufficient. Corrupted oversized pointer files gracefully return `null` (already handled by the existing try-catch).

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: pointerPath, maxBytes: TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES })` at `src/trajectory/cleanup.ts:65-69`
- Added `TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`

target.title: fix(provider-usage): parse MiniMax remaining-percent usage payload
target.body:
Closes #110887

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw status` (or the Usage dashboard) with a MiniMax coding-plan / portal key would see **MiniMax: Unsupported response shape** even though the live `/v1/token_plan/remains` call succeeds and returns billing data.

Affected surface: provider usage summary for MiniMax (`minimax` / `minimax-portal` status and usage views).

## Why This Change Was Made

MiniMax’s current coding-plan payload uses top-level `model_remains` entries named `general` / `video` with zero interval totals and remaining quota expressed as `current_interval_remaining_percent` / `current_weekly_remaining_percent`. The shared MiniMax usage fetcher only selected `MiniMax-M*` records with positive totals and only inverted legacy `usage_percent` fields, so every candidate failed and status reported an unsupported shape.

This change keeps the shared fetcher additive: prefer chat/general records that carry recognized remaining-percent fields, derive used percent from interval then weekly remaining percent (legacy `usage_percent` still works), and add a regression fixture for the reported live payload. No new config knobs; configured `baseUrl` origin handling is unchanged.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — additive field recognition only, existing count-based fixtures preserved; performance — same request path, small extra key scans; usability — status shows real usage percent instead of a false error; security — no auth/secret handling changes.

## User Impact

Operators with MiniMax portal/coding-plan credentials see a normal MiniMax usage window (percent used, window label, reset time) on status/usage surfaces instead of a permanent “Unsupported response shape” error for the current API shape.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

Focused tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.minimax.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.test.ts
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.minimax.test.ts (21 tests)
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/provider-usage.test.ts (6 tests)
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  27 passed (27)
```

Static substitutes after `pnpm check:changed` expanded into plugin-sdk dts regen (heavy expansion):

```text
git diff --check  # clean
oxfmt --check src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.minimax.ts src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.minimax.test.ts  # correct format
oxlint … on the two touched files  # 0 warnings / 0 errors
```

`pnpm check:changed` progressed through docs/guards and core typecheck before lint spawned plugin-sdk declaration rebuild; quality floor covered via path-scoped static + focused Vitest above.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MiniMax usage fetcher must accept the live coding-plan `model_remains` payload (`general` + remaining-percent fields, zero totals) and return a used-percent window instead of `Unsupported response shape`.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at this PR head; mocked HTTP response via production `fetchMinimaxUsage` (no live MiniMax credentials required).
- Current-main contrast: On main, feeding the issue’s reported top-level `model_remains` payload (general @ 97% interval remaining, video @ 100%) yields `{ error: "Unsupported response shape", windows: [] }` because `pickChatModelRemains` drops zero-total records and `deriveUsedPercent` ignores `current_interval_remaining_percent`.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` spawns the QA CLI as a detached child and attaches `data` listeners to its `stdout`/`stderr`, but never removed them. After the child closed, the retained listeners kept the stream references alive longer than necessary — a child-process lifecycle cleanup gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `close`, detach both stdio `data` listeners (`child.stdout.off("data", onStdout)` / `child.stderr.off("data", onStderr)`). The handlers are named functions so the exact references can be removed. An earlier unconditional `child.unref()` was dropped per review feedback (ineffective for the cleanup goal); the close-time detachment is the retained behavior.

## User Impact

No behavior change for QA suite runs; the parent process no longer retains stdio listeners after the QA CLI child closes.

## Real behavior proof — actual detached QA CLI child run (final head, 2026-07-19)

The exported `runQaCli` was invoked directly on the PR head. It spawned a **real detached subprocess** (`node <repoRoot>/dist/index.js ...`, production spawn path with `detached: true`, piped stdio); a stub CLI stands in for the openclaw entry so the scenario is hermetic — spawn, streams, close handling, and listener cleanup are all the production code path.

```bash
time ./node_modules/.bin/tsx child-lifecycle-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:46:05 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
code path: extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts runQaCli (real detached spawn)
[success] runQaCli resolved in 52ms: {"ok":true,"argv":["memory","status","--json"]}
[failure] rejected in 46ms: qa cli failed (2): boom
[cleanup] active handles after close: Socket, Socket, Socket, ChildProcess
[cleanup] parent's own stdio Sockets plus the already-closed ChildProcess object are expected;
[cleanup] no open child stdio streams remain — the process exits on its own (see `time` below),
[cleanup] which would not happen if close-time listeners kept streams alive.

real    0m0.701s
exit=0
```

- **Success path**: child writes JSON on stdout + a warning on stderr, exits 0; `runQaCli` resolves with the parsed payload.
- **Failure path**: child exits 2; `runQaCli` rejects promptly with the stderr tail.
- **Post-close cleanup**: after both runs the parent process exits on its own in 0.7s with no explicit `process.exit` — retained close-time listeners would have kept the event loop alive.

target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws: text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`): still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Live createBrowserTool handler + browser control service (primary proof)

This is the proof ClawSweeper asked for: the changed `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot **catch** runs against a real managed Chrome tab through the in-process browser control service (not vitest mocks), configured vision fails through the real `describeImageFile` runtime, and a later `browser snapshot` in the same session stays text-only with zero image content blocks.

Reproduce (from this branch; needs local Chrome):

```
cd ~/oss-openclaw-106703   # or your checkout of fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
git checkout fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

Redacted live transcript (2026-07-18, head `e1fba23acb5`; no base64 bytes, no private paths):

```
=== Step 1: start browser (real browser control service) ===

=== Step 2: open proof page (real browser control service) ===
opened tab targetId: [redacted-tab-id]
proof page url: https://example.com/

=== Step 3: screenshot via real createBrowserTool().execute() (configured vision fails) ===
[media-understanding] image: failed (0/1) reason=Unknown model
--- real screenshot handler catch path ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini]
[Screenshot saved to "[redacted-path]/outbound/[redacted].png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
details.vision.failed: true
details.vision.error: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini

=== Step 4: later snapshot in same session (real handler) ===
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: (wrapped external browser snapshot text; truncated)

result: PASS
```

To force a provider HTTP failure instead of model resolution (401/503 from a real endpoint), set a valid configured model ref plus an invalid key before running the script:

```
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-invalid-proof-key-replace-me
# ensure models.providers.openai.models includes your image model in the runtime config the script loads
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

### Real-handler behavioral proof (vitest; mocked vision throw only)

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: on a configured image-understanding failure the screenshot tool result previously carried a raw base64 image block, which is retained across recent completed turns (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages` keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns) and forces later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` results into image-analysis framing until `/new`.

The proof drives the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot handler with the configured image-understanding call (`describeImageFile`) forced to fail, then drives a later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler. Only the vision call is mocked (to throw); the screenshot handler, its catch path, and the surrounding tool flow are real production code. It lives in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` under the describe block `browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof (#106703, #105305)`.

Reproduce:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts -t "browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof" --disableConsoleIntercept
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types and image-block counts only; no base64 bytes are printed):

```
--- real screenshot handler (configured vision failure) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: vision provider unavailable (HTTP 503)] \n [Screenshot saved to "/tmp/openclaw-media/outbound/share.png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: <<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="browser">>> \n ok \n <<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>
=== session transcript (redacted) ===
user: screenshot the dashboard and summarize it
toolResult(browser:screenshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: the configured vision model was unavailable
user: now read the deploy status file
toolResult(read): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: deploy is green
user: take a page snapshot
toolResult(browser:snapshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: captured snapshot
total image content blocks across session: 0
--- no-vision path (unchanged) screenshot result ---
content-block types: [text, image]
image content blocks: 1
text: browser:screenshot
```

Reading the transcript:

- Real screenshot handler with configured vision forced to fail: the emitted tool result is text-only (`image content blocks: 0`), carries the neutralized failure reason and the staged outbound-copy share hint, and sets `details.vision.failed` with no `details.media`.
- A later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler stays text-framed, and the reconstructed multi-turn session carries `total image content blocks: 0`, so nothing base64 rides alongside later `read` / `snapshot` results.
- No-vision path (unchanged): the same handler still reaches `imageResultFromFile` and emits a base64 image block (`image content blocks: 1`). This is the exact tool-result shape the pre-fix catch produced and that `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` preserves for recent turns, so the mechanism is real and the fix is scoped to the configured-vision-failure catch.

Honesty note: the vitest proof mocks only the single vision throw to isolate handler output shapes. The live handler script above uses real Chrome, the real browser control service, the real changed catch path, and the real `describeImageFile` runtime (no mock).

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path:

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

### Local gate (redacted)

```
vitest extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts                          100 passed
vitest extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.test.ts                          6 passed
vitest src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts      12 passed
lint:extensions                                                             clean
format:check                                                                clean
tsgo:extensions:test                                                        0 errors
deadcode:full (knip production + all-exports)                               clean  (resolves check-dependencies unused-file)
live handler proof (scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts)   PASS
```

Closes #106703
Related #105305

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron output jobs targeting `current` or `session:<id>` could miss their initial announce delivery when created through the direct service path. Normalization and runtime planning already treated those targets like `isolated`, so behavior depended on which creation path was used.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer rewrite gives the invariant one owner: `shouldDefaultCronDeliveryToAnnounce()` is used by create normalization, direct-service persistence, and runtime delivery planning. It covers `agentTurn` and `command` jobs targeting `isolated`, `current`, or `session:<id>`.

Explicit delivery remains authoritative. Omitted output targets still canonicalize to `isolated`; `main` and `systemEvent` behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Current-session and named-session cron output jobs now default consistently to announce instead of silently dropping their result in one creation path.

## Release Note

Cron initial delivery now defaults current and named-session output jobs to announce consistently across normalized, direct-service, and declarative creation paths. Thanks @cxbAsDev.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `8de9484f94928`
- Blacksmith Testbox: 175 focused cron contract tests passed on the final behavior change.
- Blacksmith Testbox: full changed gates, test types, and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview after the final main merge: no findings, confidence 0.96.
- Exact-head hosted CI was green before the release-owned changelog bullet was removed; the resulting source/test diff is unchanged and CI is rerun on this final head.

The focused suites cover normalization, direct `CronService.add` persistence, declarative convergence, runtime planning, omitted-target canonicalization, current and named-session targets, both output payload kinds, and explicit-delivery preservation.

## Compatibility

This restores the existing delivery default consistently. It adds no config, protocol, storage, or migration surface.

target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session upstream monitor resolved catalog providers from the **mutable** plugin registry state (`getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry`). When a standalone plugin load swaps that registry, the monitor can silently lose sight of the providers backing adopted-session upstream watches — upstream activity for watched sessions stops being observed until the next registry churn happens to restore them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch the monitor's provider source to the **pinned** session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry`), the same source the session-catalog path already trusts. The pinned registry survives mutable-registry swaps, so watched upstream links keep resolving to their catalog providers across plugin reloads.

## User Impact

Adopted-session upstream monitoring keeps working across plugin registry churn instead of intermittently missing upstream activity. No configuration or API change.

## Real behavior proof — multi-plugin registry churn (final head `c8be3d57`, 2026-07-19)

Runtime trace executing the **real** plugin runtime (`src/plugins/runtime.ts`), state database (SQLite in a temp state dir), and the real monitor tick (`src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts`) — no mocks of the monitor or registry plumbing. The pinned registry carries **two** providers; the mutable registry is churned twice, the second time with a rogue provider that must never be consulted.

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx registry-churn-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:38:22 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
modules: src/plugins/runtime.ts + src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts @ PR head
state dir: /var/folders/…/openclaw-pinned-registry-proof-Sex0IS
[setup] mutable active registry swapped in (empty — simulates plugin reload churn)
[setup] pinned session-extension registry carries providers: "claude", "codex"
[setup] watched catalogs: claude, codex
[tick 1] before churn:
  -> provider "claude" checkUpstreamActivity called with 1 probe(s)
  -> provider "codex" checkUpstreamActivity called with 1 probe(s)
[churn] mutable active registry replaced; now carries only "rogue"
[tick 2] after churn:
  -> provider "claude" checkUpstreamActivity called with 1 probe(s)
  -> provider "codex" checkUpstreamActivity called with 1 probe(s)
[result] provider calls: ["claude","codex","claude","codex"]
[result] PASS: monitor kept using the pinned providers across churn; rogue never called
```

Both pinned providers are consulted on every tick; the mutable registry's contents (empty first, then a rogue provider) never influence the monitor.

## Regression tests (final head)

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts
```

```

## What was not tested

A full multi-plugin Gateway process trace (with real plugin hosts and model providers) was not produced — the trace above runs the exact monitor and registry code paths against a real state database, which is where the provider-source selection lives. No endpoints, credentials, or room IDs involved, so nothing required redaction.

target.title: fix(ci): skip Periphery scans for unrelated PR changes
target.body:
Related: #106090
Observed on: #106789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. The stale event base SHA made base-branch changes look like pull-request changes, consuming macOS runners and adding irrelevant checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three Periphery scope jobs now compare GitHub's synthetic pull-request merge commit with its first parent, which is the exact base tree used to build that merge result. Checkout depth is increased to two so both commits are available; the stale event-base fetch is no longer needed.

Scope behavior remains fail-closed, manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, and renamed files remain covered.

## User Impact

Unrelated pull requests no longer start iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit Periphery scan jobs solely because `main` changed. Pull requests that actually touch the scoped native paths continue to run the same scans.

AI-assisted change; I reviewed and understand the implementation and tests.

## Evidence

- Regression test builds a hermetic synthetic merge where `main` adds a shared OpenClawKit file while the PR changes only docs. The old event-base comparison reports a scoped change; `HEAD^1..HEAD` reports only the PR's docs file and sets `should-scan=false`.
